summary: 100-foot steel tower in Bankhead National Forest, Lawrence County, built 1929-30 and NHLR-registered 2023; a visitor kiosk is nearby, climbing access unconfirmed.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower; NHLR says not an Aermotor and probably by the International Derrick Company (unconfirmed)

access.note: Visitor kiosk site near the tower; no source says whether the tower may be climbed

visit.trail_note: Kiosk near the tower on AL Highway 33, about 11.4 miles south of Moulton, per the Alabama Birding Trails guide

events.note: Newspapers describe construction in 1929 and near completion by October; NHLR gives 1930 or earlier and cites a 1930 map
Silas Black named as keeper of the tower
Mollie Downing climbs to the top; reported June 26, 1930
Frank Armor named chief observer for the Third Army aircraft-warning service during May maneuvers (planned, per April 1940 report)

corrections.why: Birmingham News reports from 1929 describe the tower under construction and nearing completion; NHLR says 1930 or earlier. The 1929 date is the earliest documented; treat as medium confidence.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says 1930 or earlier and cites a 1930 map; 1929 newspapers describe construction and near completion. The record uses 1929 as the earliest documented year and the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Brief elevation 303.6 m matches NHLR 996 ft (304 m); an OpenStreetMap node shows 299 m and was not used. Standing status rests on the NHLR site visit of 26 November 2022; no later check found. Climbing access is not stated in any source read; the birding guide gives only the kiosk. The anyplaceamerica.com listing returned HTTP 403 and was not used.
